claims.text: The anomalous ductile-brittle-ductile transition between 550 and 750°C is driven by coupled evolution of L12 ordered domains and jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries.
Aging near 600°C produces excessive, near-Ni3Al-stoichiometric chemical ordering in the FCC matrix.
The increased L12 ordering near 600°C significantly raises the antiphase boundary energy.
High antiphase boundary energy restricts dislocation cross-slip and promotes planar slip.
Jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries concentrate stress and promote crack initiation and brittle failure.
Aging near 750°C reduces the degree of L12 ordering and lowers the antiphase boundary energy.
The lower antiphase boundary energy at 750°C permits cross-slip and ductile deformation.
Aging near 750°C forms ductile transition zones along phase boundaries.
The critical transition boundary is the onset of near-stoichiometric Ni3Al-like L12 ordering combined with sufficiently jagged phase boundaries.
The as-cast alloy has a dual-phase lamellar microstructure containing FCC-L12 and BCC-B2 phases.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 750 MPa.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a room-temperature elongation of approximately 18%.
Aging near 600°C causes a sharp loss of elongation and produces a brittle state.
The 600°C-aged material fractures by intergranular or phase-boundary cracking.
Aging near 750°C restores elongation to near the as-cast level.
Nanoindentation at jagged boundaries in the 600°C-aged sample should show higher hardness and a smaller plastic zone than in the 750°C-aged sample.
TEM of the 600°C-aged sample should show planar slip bands and antiphase-boundary-related defects.
TEM of the 750°C-aged sample should show wavy slip, reduced ordering, and ductile transition zones.
Jagged phase boundaries should be present at 600°C and absent or smoother at 750°C.
Samples are proposed to be aged for 100-500 hours in an inert atmosphere or vacuum.
